The Congress hit the BJP where it hurt the most by winning the most prestigious Nagpur seat, the only seat it could win across all the States which went to polls. title: Tanker with 27 Indian seafarers targeted in first-ever limpet mine attack in Hormuz
description: On October 29 and 30, two oil tankers were targeted in separate attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. MT LOUISE 1 was struck by limpet mines that caused a fire in its engine room. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil export routes, connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It has faced repeated security incidents since the conflict between US and Iran began.

title: Father's death, a promise and Worlds gold: Manisha Bhanwala's story

But behind this historic achievement was a personal story of loss, family sacrifices and a promise she had made to herself.

title: 'I want teams to fear Mumbai Indians even when we play away': New batting coach
description: Mumbai Indians batting coach Robin Uthappa wants the team to become a force not just at the Wankhede Stadium but also at every other venue in the IPL. He believes the five-time champions must win back the trust of their fans after a disappointing 2025 season. Mumbai Indians finished ninth among 10 teams in IPL 2025. Uthappa knows the team, under head coach Kieron Pollard, has a lot of work to do to return to its winning ways.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf donate $1 million to Las Vegas charity
description: In a heartwarming display of philanthropy, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf pledged $1 million at a charity gala, bolstering the efforts of Keep Memory Alive, which benefits the Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health. Agassi was honored for his charitable influence during the event in Las Vegas. This recent contribution adds to their previous donation of $1.5 million, bringing their total support to an impressive $2.

title: Reliance Q2 results: RIL posts record Rs 29,550 crore quarterly profit
description: Reliance Industries Limited announced impressive figures for FY27, with consolidated gross revenue peaking at Rs 3,62,268 crore. The company experienced a remarkable profit growth of 33.8%, reaching Rs 29,550 crore, largely due to a stellar 67.9% rise in oil-to-chemicals segment EBITDA. While retail revenue saw a 6.4% improvement, challenges persisted in that sector. Moreover, the quarter's capital expenditure of Rs 38,153 crore predominantly targeted O2C and New Energy.

title: Two days of rain bring Delhi’s AQI down to 60; minister credits ‘targeted action’
description: Delhi has experienced significant improvements in air quality due to recent rainfall and government initiatives. The average Air Quality Index for October was lower compared to previous years. Rainfall contributed significantly, with over eight times the normal monthly amount recorded. Public participation in anti-pollution measures is acknowledged by officials as a vital factor for change.

title: BJP plans counter-protest against oppn's march, 1984 anti-Sikh riots to be in focus
Two friends turn $15 Denver haunted house into 18 Halloween attractions
description: Two friends, Chris Stafford and Warren Conard, opened a haunted house in a Denver shopping complex in 2002, charging $15 per ticket. What began as a side business has grown into a multimillion-dollar company with 18 seasonal Halloween attractions across the US. The company paid around 4,500 workers during the 2025 Halloween season and is now expanding into Christmas entertainment.

title: Meet Landon Hoberman: Teen’s campaign prevents 8.1 million plastic utensils
description: Landon Hoberman, a 17-year-old from New Jersey, has made remarkable strides in reducing plastic cutlery usage in restaurants. His campaign has succeeded in keeping over 8 million utensils out of landfills, while restaurants collectively saved more than $200,000 by making cutlery optional for takeaway. This initiative showcases how small changes can lead to significant environmental impact and financial savings, presenting a scalable model for communities seeking to tackle single-use plastics.

title: Jharkhand women turn Rs 2 savings into Rs 6 lakh ragi collective
description: Kunwari Barwa's initiatives began with a self-help group where women saved small amounts of money together. As the group expanded, they formed a farmer producer organisation focused on ragi cultivation and product sales. The collective now boasts 1,501 members and generates monthly sales of Rs 6 lakh to Rs 7 lakh. Women involved gain employment opportunities and experience market exposure through fairs and exhibitions beyond their village.

title: Manisha Bhanwala becomes India's first women's world wrestling champion
description: In a breathtaking gold medal bout, Manisha overturned a daunting 0-6 deficit to defeat Pan American champion Abigail Nette 8-6. Refusing to surrender despite falling behind early, the Indian wrestler mounted a remarkable comeback to turn the contest on its head and secure a historic victory.

title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
description: AISA leader Neha Bora's refusal to sign peace bonds led to obvious comparisions with the CJP leadership who opted to comply with conditions set for their release from detention during Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests. The CJP faced significant challenges in organizing Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests which was a contrast from their previous successful mobilization. Bora's determination to protest despite multiple detentions brought her to the centre stage of anti-SIR protests.

title: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia appointed IAF vice-chief
Payday to mayday: The hike mirage and why bigger salaries still feel smaller
description: In India, salary increases of approximately 9% are falling short against the backdrop of soaring living costs and inflation. Families are grappling with heightened expenses on essentials like food and fuel, resulting in diminished disposable incomes. This widening gap between income growth and the cost of living places a strain on households, particularly those with fixed financial obligations.

title: Paid to hire, paid to work: Inside India’s Rs 99,446 cr plan to reshape formal workforce
description: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is introduced to enhance formal employment across various sectors. The scheme includes financial incentives for both employers and first-time employees entering the formal job market. PMVBRY aims to create more than 3.5 crore jobs including 1.92 crore first-time workers by 2027. It targets an increase in manufacturing employment with unique incentives for the sector.

title: Melinda French Gates says her 2-day rule helps employees know they did a good job
description: Melinda French Gates implements a 48-hour feedback rule for employees to manage work conflicts effectively. This approach allows employees to feel secure in their performance evaluations as surprises are avoided. She emphasizes the importance of giving honest feedback with integrity while maintaining respect. Recently, Gates pledged $215 million to improve women's health and called for better accountability in healthcare systems.

title: Dravid, Sehwag named in India squad for U19 Asia Cup
description: Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag have been named in India's squad for the upcoming ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup. The tournament will be held in Muscat, Oman, from November 5 to 14. The 17-year-old Anvay and 19-year-old Aaryavir earned their places after impressive performances in the recently concluded Vinoo Mankad Trophy.

title: Why kids forget to brush their teeth after being told, according to psychology
description: Getting children ready in the morning can be challenging due to their developing memory skills, which are essential for task completion. Observations reveal that children often forget instructions as their attention shifts to other activities. Strategies such as providing visual reminders and making tasks more engaging can significantly help enhance their memory. Additionally, encouraging children to think ahead can promote greater responsibility in completing tasks.

title: $6.3bn gone in 20 mins: How North Korean hackers pulled off biggest crypto heist
description: Hackers executed the largest theft in cryptocurrency history by stealing $6.36 billion from Binance wallets. The theft involved moving funds across 10 blockchains in a short time span. TRM Labs has linked the attack to TraderTraitor, an elite hacking unit from North Korea. Binance has committed to covering all losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users.

title: Hasina video, RAW links: What ex-Bangladesh officer revealed before mysterious death
Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $325M KC Current opens soccer doors for kids
description: The Kansas City Current launched a free youth soccer league in July to help children overcome financial barriers to sports. The program provides 120 players aged 8 to 10 with uniforms, Nike cleats and equipment at no cost. Supported by community partners, the initiative also offers coach stipends and referee training for teenagers. The league aims to expand access, support local families and encourage greater participation, particularly among girls.

title: Mississippi court backs father's deed giving family land to wife over children
description: A Mississippi father left his family home and 0.86 acres of land equally to his three children in a 2008 will but transferred the property to his wife in 2021. After his death, his daughter challenged the transfer, claiming he had been improperly influenced due to his declining health. On Tuesday, an appeals court rejected her challenge, finding insufficient evidence of undue influence.

title: California couple wins garden rights after neighbour’s 1955 deal for $250
description: A California couple who bought a home in 2019 found themselves in a legal battle after their neighbour claimed ownership of a 20-by-20-foot garden they believed was theirs. The dispute centred on a 1955 agreement involving $250, babysitting services and land access rights. On Monday, a California appeals court upheld the couple's exclusive right to use the garden.
